references.text: Parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says the same thing: "If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me."
Parallel passage in Mark where Jesus speaks to the crowd and disciples with the same message about denying oneself, taking up one's cross, and following Him.

Jesus repeats similar words later in Luke: "Whoever does not carry their own cross and come after me cannot be my disciple." This elaborates on the requirement of cross-bearing as a condition for discipleship.
Jesus says: "Whoever does not take up their cross and follow me is not worthy of me." An earlier statement in Matthew with the same theme of cross-bearing and discipleship.
Paul writes that if we live according to the flesh, we will die, but if by the Spirit we put to death the deeds of the body, we will live. This expresses denying oneself in practice.
Paul says: "I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me." This is a practical outworking of denying oneself and taking up one's cross daily.
"Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires." Taking up one's cross daily involves crucifying the old self.
Paul says that he will boast in nothing except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by which the world has been crucified to him and he to the world. The cross as a principle of life.
"We know that our old self was crucified with Him." Denying oneself and taking up one's cross daily is theologically grounded in connection with Christ's crucifixion.
Paul speaks tearfully about those who are enemies of the cross of Christ – a contrast to those who take up their cross daily and follow Jesus.

The immediately following verse elaborates on the meaning: whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for Jesus' sake will save it. This explains what it means to deny oneself.
John urges us not to love the world or anything in the world. Denying oneself daily involves turning away from worldly desires.
Jesus' reasoning for self-denial: "For whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for my sake will find it."
